title: The swallow-family census's header describes the #12981 handover as pending, and counts the gate vocabulary at 18, after that handover landed
body:
The census `scripts/measure-durability-swallow-family.mjs` is the instrument of record for the #12981 programme, and its header describes that programme's handover step in the FUTURE tense:

> ## The handover (the ruling's LAST step, not this one)
>
> The programme ends by adding the seeder-helper names (`tryInsert`/`tryUpdate`) to the gate's `DURABILITY_CRITICAL_CALLEES` **with zero reds** ...

PR #15458 performs that step. Three statements in the header go stale with it, none of them mechanically checked by anything:

1. **The section reads as pending when it has landed.** A future-tense "the programme ends by X" over an X that already happened is the exact class of lie carrier this instrument's own `DETERMINED` register was built to prevent one layer down.
2. **"an 18-entry `DURABILITY_CRITICAL_CALLEES` vocabulary"** (header, "The premise the census carries") is 20 after that PR. The sentence beside it — that a seeder reaching storage through `ql.insert(...)` is not in the vocabulary — stays true.
3. **The `origin` labels for `tryInsert` / `tryUpdate` now overlap.** `WRITE_SHAPED_CALLEES` marks them `seed-wrapper` ("the names the ruling's last step hands to the gate"), while `gate-vocabulary` is defined as "already declared in `check-durability-degradation-log-level.mjs`" — which, after that PR, they are.

## Why this is filed and not fixed in the same PR

Item 3 is not mechanical: moving those two rows to `gate-vocabulary` would change what the census reports as the gate/census OVERLAP, i.e. a reading, not a comment. That is a judgement about the instrument, and this instrument is the shared measurement device of a programme in flight — the same reason the earlier census-heading defect was filed rather than repaired in-batch. Items 1 and 2 are authorial prose for whoever makes that call.

⛔ Not a behaviour defect: the census's output, its self-test and its controls are all green and unchanged by #15458 (the reading is byte-identical before and after, because the census copies the gate's vocabulary by value on purpose).

Found while landing batch 10 of #12981. Unassigned.
